chapter: Own bands and Los Angeles clubs
title: Leading the house band at The Oasis; Billy Eckstine and Mingus
summary: Lee led the Oasis house band for about two years, backing Louis, Nat, Billie Holiday and Eckstine, whose song Mingus interrupted with his bow.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: When it was the Florentine Gardens, they used to work there all the time. But now after that, happened, I think this was when The Oasis came in to, like '50 and '51, '52 ...
You had the first house band there, didn't you?

Yes, I had the house band and we were there maybe two years, like, and this is when Louis would come in, and Nat would come in, and Lady Day would come in -- all the big acts would come. Frankie Lane and let's see who else ...
Had Eddie [Deshields] sold it by then?
Oh no. No. Eddie was still ...

No, he owned it when I was there, and what's the girl who was the singer with one of the bands -- Anita O'Day played there, and as I said, Frankie Lane and Billy Eckstine was there. They had all the -- and Mingus was playing there with me. I had Mingus in the band there, and I never will forget; Billy is out on the floor doing "Old Man River", and Mingus used to love to bow his bass, you know.

And so Billy's trying to sing, people all singing the verse of the thing, and back in the back, Mingus is sawing on this thing -- he's gonna do a concerto on it, you know. And Billy just turned around and said, "Put the spotlight on him!"
So, you know, Mingus was kind of a character.
